purpose: Find whether cross-seed split/merge incompatibility can be repaired by compact joint native groups anchored to source-only features.
scope: Exposed natural discovery8192 and calibration4096 tokens, one shared seed edge, two controlled SAE mechanisms. Source anchors selected solely from source activity and energy quantiles. Joint groups fit actual nonnegative zero-ablation contributions, with independent mean/Phi reported separately. Soft gates in[0,1], anchor fixed1, bounded convex quadratic and standard L-BFGS-B. Calibration is development feedback, not fresh confirmation. Group correspondence error is not yet a measured finite model effect or semantic certificate. Best-atom comparator applies to exactly the same learned source group; anchored-atom comparison changes source granularity and is reported as such. Also evaluate actual full-LM zero ablations on source-selected active and uniform calibration contexts; compare the same source group with a target group, best target atom, rank1/rank2 compression and shuffled-context control. These are all exposed development contexts, not fresh confirmation. The first operator-only run had complete scientific arrays but missed the raw hash field in its summary; corrected in place with original metadata preserved.
recovery: v2 failed before any functional endpoint because cached hidden states were produced with high matmul precision, but the new quadratic driver retained highest. Match original high precision and full16-row producer shape, padding final evaluation batches; omit the one incomplete original producer block before source-only context selection.
